title: You asked for more transparency in AI trading results. Here’s my first performance snapshot.
author: xMavchartAI
selftext:
A few days ago, I shared an XAUUSD analysis from xMav Chart AI, and several traders asked for more transparent performance tracking.  
Here’s an early snapshot from the app:  
📊 80 analyses recorded  
✅ 17 TP  
❌ 2 SL  
⏳ 61 WAIT  
The 89% figure is calculated from 19 selected setups. I manually checked their outcomes against market charts.  
These are self-reported observations, not independently audited results or executed trades. The sample is small and may not represent the AI’s overall accuracy.  
The app already saves previous analyses, and I’m exploring how to make their outcomes more transparent and publicly verifiable.  
What additional data would you want to see in a public performance log?

comments.author: Successful-Mud-2000
comments.body:
Respect for adding the disclaimers, most people dont. Since you asked what I would want to see, honestly the key word for me is "selected". If you picked 19 out of 80 to check, the 89% doesnt really tell us much



What would make it believable:



Every single signal, not a selection. All 80, including the 61 WAIT. What happened to those? If price moved without them triggering that matters too



Signals published before the outcome, with a timestamp nobody can edit. Entry, SL, TP and time all fixed at the moment the AI gave it. Posting them live in a public channel works, or even a hash of each signal



A clear rule for when a signal expires, so old setups dont get counted as wins days later



Results in R, not just win rate. With 89% wins and almost 2R per win the expectancy would be insane, so if it holds over a big sample that alone would be the headline



At least 100 to 200 closed signals in different conditions, not just one trending week in gold



If the numbers still look good after all that, people will trust it way more than any screenshot

replies.author: xMavchartAI
replies.body:
Really appreciate the detailed feedback!  
Just to clarify, the 61 WAIT results are cases where the AI suggested not entering a trade. The other 19 setups were manually reviewed against market charts.  
You’re absolutely right that 19 setups aren’t enough to establish reliability.  
The app already saves analysis history, but a proper public performance log should include every analysis, timestamps, predefined expiry rules, and results measured in R.  
That’s a valuable direction for improving transparency as more data becomes available.  
Thanks for the constructive feedback! 🚀

replies.author: Successful-Mud-2000
replies.body:
Thanks for clarifying, that changes it. If the 19 are all the times the AI said enter then its not a selection, my bad on that part

Two small things I would still add:

The WAITs can be tracked too. If the AI says dont enter and price would have hit SL, thats a good call. If it would have hit TP, thats a missed trade. Over time that tells you if the filter is actually adding value

And I would automate the outcome check instead of reviewing charts by hand. Not saying you are doing it wrong, just that a script checking if SL or TP got hit first removes any doubt

Looking forward to the next update

replies.author: xMavchartAI
replies.body:
Those are actually two great suggestions!  
Tracking WAIT outcomes could help measure how useful the AI’s filtering really is, and automating TP/SL verification would make the results much more objective.  
Both are definitely worth exploring for future updates.  
Really appreciate the thoughtful feedback and support! 🚀

comments.author: Leomantry
comments.body: looks dope, one ask is if there’s a way to change it to english in the app?

replies.author: xMavchartAI
replies.body:
Not yet, but English support is definitely on the roadmap! I’m planning to add it to both the iOS app and the web version.  
Really appreciate the feedback! 🙌🚀
